text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- The cabinet postponed its regular Thursday meetings once more. It last met on April 2, following a meeting of the military-dominated National Security Council (MGK), which has demanded the Islamist-conservative coalition crack down on Islamist zeal.
- Turkish tycoon Sakip Sabanci says he is fed up with all five party leaders in parliament.
HURRIYET

- Conservative and leftist opposition leaders say they have agreed on a three-way coalition government formula which would be headed by the current junior coalition partner, in a bid to exclude Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamists from power.
- Fujitsu, a Japanese computer company, says that high inflation and and unstable economy does not put them off investing in Turkey -- on the contrary, they believe it serves to increase their sales.
MILLIYET

- Erbakan states his disapproval of a plan for eight years of uninterrupted compulsory education by saying vocational high-school education should begin early. The call for the implementing of the was one of the MGK demands designed to curb Islamist activism. Under this plan the first section of the religious schools would effectively be shut down.
- A section of a thermal plant in Kutahya province blew up and turned a 18 kilometers of land into a desert. The damage is estimated at $2.9 million.
YENI YUZYIL

- The deputy chairman of the Erbakan's Welfare Party, Ahmet Tekdal warns governors against closing down private Moslem religious teaching centres in accordance with a demand by the conservative interior minister.
- The foreign trade deficit for the first nine months of 1997 is announced as $13.4 billion.
RADIKAL
- State minister Sabri Tekir says Turkish businessmen have $29 billion invested in Swiss banks.
- Claudia Roth, the chair of the Green Party in the European Parliament and a regular visitor to Turkey, says she wants to help establish democracy in Turkey.
CUMHURIYET
- A parliamentary commission approves the employment of 17,000 extra people for the General Directorate of Religious Affairs.
ZAMAN
- More than 140 Non-governmental Organisations met Erbakan to urge his party not to accept the eight-year uninterrupted compulsory education plan.
DUNYA
- The association of Turkish businessmen in Europe will own 45 percent of a new Turkish bank to open soon in Germany.
- The milk industry lost $2,900 last month after lowering its prices to increase demand.
